title: How to create a State that makes players un-revivable in battle?

posts.author: emma_watson
posts.body:
Hi, there is a cool outfit in my game that has certain capabilities, but the stipulation is that the
character will be unable to get revived.  Permadeath.
The only end result of a battle is
winning or getting a game over
.
Does anyone know a way to achieve this? Thanks in advance. Preferably I wanted to know if this is somehow doable without using a plugin, however, if that's the only option, I'd love a recommendation of some sort. Thanks for reading.

im not sure if its easily doable without plugins, but i use a few yanfly plugins to pull off a similar effect.
the main one for me is the the

plugin so that i can designate certain states to persist on death. But since yours is a gear effect, you can use the

skill core
plugin to make it so that all revival items revive through the notebox, and then make them fail to work on targets with the denial state on.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Most likely you'll have to use a plugin.
There are some ways the engine can be redirected or tricked, but they usually have other restrictions and are difficult to implement with such a specific case.
The only alternative I can think of at the moment would be to change all revival items and skills to call a common event instead of having a direct effect, then in the common event check if the target has that equipment and if not, revive by event commands.
But that will require some length of event code that gets more complex the more actors and the more revival options you have.

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
Are you also going to have normal death from which actors can be revived?
If you want both normal and permadeath, you might find Himework's Custom Death states useful:
https://himeworks.com/2015/11/custom-death-states/
Not used it myself, but it should treat the states that you choose as if they are State 1 (death).
If you have normal and permadeath you might try running battle events every turn to check whether the actor prone to permadeath is dead, and either adding another state or replacing the death state with the permadeath state.
What may be useful, whether or not you have both permadeath and normal death, is to have a common event parallel process to check the party every few seconds for certain states and remove the affected actor(s) from the party. [Note that parallel common events stop working during combat.] I don't have permadeath in my games, but I move the dead actors to another party so that it is easy to revive them later. (I use Himework's Party Manager to allow more than one party.) You might just check for permadeath, if you are happy with the way normal death is handled.

posts.author: Prescott
posts.body:
Run a check in battles where, if an actor's HP is 0 and they're wearing the outfit, it applies another state to them. You can make this state the same as the default Dead one, and use the Traits to force the character with that state to always have 0 HP or the default Dead state so they'll just keep dying again if you try to bring them back. Only downside to this method is that you'll still be able to use revival items on them which will lead to the player wasting them, although that could be kind of interesting from a narrative standpoint (not even revival items will bring them back).
Although, why keep the permadeath'd character in the party at all? Just remove them from the party if they hit 0 HP while wearing the outfit. That's much more elegant. Though I guess the downside to that is that you also immediately lose everything that party member had equipped, including the outfit. Could maybe find a way to work that in to the outfit's description or lore, though. The person who wears it alongside all their belongings will turn to ash if they reach 0 HP, something like that. Could even put an item in the party's inventory of the dead party member's ashes. Maybe they can use those ashes for something else! I'm getting ahead of myself though.

posts.author: ZimXero
posts.body:
IF the expert coders don't come up with something... I think B3N4ZC4L's idea holds potential.  Suppose the character's name is Ned.  You will probably want dead Ned's equipment back.   Run a small script to check if Ned is ever dead in battle.  If so it triggers a variable switch.  Run a parallel event that checks the death switch out of battle.  If it's on, it changes his player icon to a tombstone, removes Ned's equipment, removes Ned from party, and triggers a story notification or sequence.
He could still be revived in battle, but maybe you could turn this glitch into a feature/cookie.  If the death switch is on, the party becomes buffed with "Ned's Last Stand" and if Ned is revived, he gains haste, and double defense until the end of his final battle.

Click to expand...
Bypass Death Removal only applies to states, not skills. its how you specify that a state can be applied to a dead battler and that when they die, its not a state that should be removed on death. the idea is that since the permadeath state wouldnt be removable by dying, it would be easy to make revives not be able to work on actors with it active.
is it a specific actor who gets this outfit applied to them? you probably wont be needing the states category plugin if it is. its the only paid plugin of the bunch i mentioned and you didnt say if you owned it. passives because of how theyre written already persist through death, which is one reason i mentioned it alongside the states categories plugin.
if its for one actor and you use a switch, you can go the passive route easily. give the actor the "Permadeath" state as a passive effect and give it the condition
Code:
<Custom Passive Condition>
condition = $gameParty.inBattle() && $gameSwitches.value(x);
</Custom Passive Condition>
replace the x for the id of the switch you flipped for the outfit and the state should be on the actor so long as theyre in battle and the switch is active.
then for your revive items/skills youd make sure the scope is dead allies, remove the damage formula and effects, and put this in its notebox
Code:
<After Eval>
if (!target.isStateAffected(y)){
  target.removeState(1);
  target.gainHp(Math.ceil(target.mhp*.25));
}
</After Eval>
replace the y for the id of the "Permadeath" state. now the revives should revive a dead ally with 25% of their max hp, but only if they dont have the "Permadeath" state active
The Selection Control plugin Turan mentioned would replace the need for the above tag and you'd just need to make the skills not be able to select battlers with the state. Its a good solution too and lets you keep the formula and effects because you just wont be able to use the revive on the actor entirely and the player wont be able to waste the item/skill cost. it too, is a paid plugin though
